data.answer:
The fall largely reflected a **bring-forward of applications into 2013** ahead of the Raising the Bar reforms, implemented in April 2013. The reforms raised the standard required for an invention to receive a patent, prompting a rush of applications before implementation and a subsequent drop that carried into 2014.[1]
IP Australia received **25,947 standard patent applications in 2014, down 13 per cent from 2013**. The 2015 report qualified its explanation, saying the decrease “may be attributed” to the reforms rather than establishing them as the sole cause.[2]

citations.quote: In April 2013 The IP Laws Amendment (Raising the Bar) Act 2012 was implemented. The new law raised the standard required for an invention to be granted a patent. This led to a rush of applications and examination requests in the weeks leading up to the implementation dates, and a resulting drop in applications for the remainder of 2013 which carried over into 2014.

claims.text: The reforms implemented in April 2013 raised patent standards, prompting applicants to bring filings forward into 2013 and contributing to the subsequent fall into 2014.

citations.quote: IP Australia received 25 947 standard patent applications in 2014, a decrease of 13 per cent relative to 2013.
The decrease in filings may be attributed to the effects of the IP Laws Amendment (Raising the Bar) Act 2012 that took force in 2013.

claims.text: Standard patent applications fell 13 per cent to 25,947 in 2014; the 2015 report qualified its attribution of the decrease to the reforms.
